docs.title: Session 0 — Fear For All
docs.text: Session: 0 — October 20, 1884 Status: Resolved

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Lacy O'Malley of the Tombstone Epitaph arranged for Father Miller, Mama Duvall, and Jim to come to Seattle. She put them in contact with the Twilight Legion's local office.

In Seattle, they met Agent Tatum Black at the Grand Central Hotel — young, overwhelmed, but sharp. He is the sole surviving agent in Seattle after two colleagues were killed in recent weeks. He laid out the situation: Seattle's Fear Level is elevated, strange events are multiplying, and reinforcements won't arrive for months. He offered the job — $10 a day for expenses and $1,000 each on completion — and gave them his list of strange events to investigate.

They also met Dr. Eliza Crowe, a Twilight Legion scientist who had come to Seattle independently to track the city's rising Fear Level using her experimental phobometer — a brass-and-glass instrument with a twitching needle. She explained how the device works and what she has observed.

Members of the O'Neil gang were encountered harassing Dr. Crowe and driven off. The gang is a criminal operation — thugs, well-organised, best treated carefully.

docs.title: Small Animal Ghosts
docs.text: Sessions: 2-3 Status: Active

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Following the Sack-Headed Man encounter, Mama Duvall befriended a coterie of small animal ghosts. They are loyal to her specifically.

Capabilities: - Scout ahead — small, unnoticed - Report observations back to Mama Duvall - Minor interference — small sounds, knocking things over, brief distractions

Limitations: - Cannot fight - Cannot interact with the physical world beyond minor interference - Loyal to Mama Duvall only — not transferable

docs.title: The Batsquatch
docs.text: Session: 7 — November 3, 1884 Status: Resolved

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Five devil bats — including a Devil Bat Queen locally nicknamed "Batsquatch" — had roosted atop the Yesler-Leery Building and were hunting lone pedestrians in the fog. Father Miller, Mama Duvall, and Jim accessed the rooftop and dealt with the threat.

During the encounter, a fire broke out and was extinguished.

docs.title: Loot
docs.text: Recovered from the rooftop aerie: victim belongings (watches, jewellery), sailor's scrimshaw piece.

docs.title: Aftermath
docs.text:
• Threat eliminated
  • Father Miller, Mama Duvall, and Jim gave an interview to Horace Clayton → November 3rd Post-Intelligencer edition

docs.title: The Broken Teeth
docs.text: Session: 5 Status: Active — unexplained

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Both Father Thomas Miller and Mama Duvall chipped a tooth on the same day, late October 1884. There is no known explanation. Neither is aware the other experienced the same thing.

docs.title: The Forgotten Train
docs.text: Status: Open — unexplained

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Father Miller, Mama Duvall, and Jim arrived in Seattle on the inbound express, October 20th, 1884. The journey was unremarkable — until it wasn't.

The third passenger car showed strange jagged scorch marks on the exterior when the train pulled into the station. The metal was buckled as if exposed to a blacksmith's forge. The conductor attributed it to a freak bush leaping from the tracks in the dead of night.

Nobody remembers anything unusual happening.

The Seattle Post-Intelligencer ran a brief sidebar in the October 22nd edition — Horace Clayton's account, which cut off mid-sentence. He noted the scorch marks. He didn't explain them either.

docs.title: What Remains Unexplained
docs.text:
• What caused the scorch marks
  • Whether the train car is still in the rail yard
  • Whether other passengers remember something that Father Miller, Mama Duvall, and Jim do not
  • Why nobody remembers

docs.title: The Haunted Hotel
docs.text: Sessions: 5-6 — Late October, 1884 Status: Resolved

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Grand Central Hotel — base of operations in Seattle — was haunted by the spirit of Giuseppe Vivaldi, a carpenter who died entombed in the hotel walls during its construction in 1880. Not evil; driven mad by decades of imprisonment. Father Miller, Mama Duvall, and Jim tracked him through the building (Room 313, the north wall, the basement furnace), demolished the bricked-up wall, and returned his toolbelt to his surviving family.

Jerome Bianchi resisted demolition but was ultimately persuaded. During the investigation, a boiler fire broke out in the basement — Mama Duvall put it out, destroying Jim's hat in the process. Giuseppe's spirit is at rest.

docs.title: Outcome
docs.text:
• Ghost laid to rest
  • Family received Vivaldi's toolbelt
  • Father Miller was gifted Vivaldi's stopwatch by the Vivaldi family (significance unclear)
  • Jim's hat: destroyed in the boiler fire. Mama Duvall is responsible. This continues.
  • Father Miller now has the trust of Seattle's Italian community
  • Jerome Bianchi is quietly, genuinely grateful

docs.title: The Priest — Father Thomas Miller
docs.text:
[!tip] Player Character Full Name: Father Thomas Miller Player: Paul Waggott Religion: Catholic Status: Alive Harrowed: No

"The Priest" is the GM/wiki alias. He is known publicly as "the Reverend Father." His telegraph identity is Father Thomas Miller.

docs.title: Player Notes
docs.text:
Submitted by Paul Waggott via Telegraph Office, 2026-04-26

Father Thomas Miller is a Catholic Priest, specialising in exorcisms and the eternal war with the forces of hell. He is in his late 40s, 6' tall, with black hair. He originally hails from the Boston area, and studied in Rome. He is a member of The Twilight Legion.

docs.title: Character Overview
docs.text: A Catholic priest operating in the Pacific Northwest. Devout. Practical about the supernatural in a way that probably unsettles his superiors back east. Has seen enough in Seattle to reframe his theology considerably.

docs.title: Physical
docs.text:
Late 40s. 6 feet tall. Black hair. Originally from Boston. Studied theology in Rome. Carries himself with the quiet authority of a man who has seen worse things than whatever is currently happening and survived them all.

Submitted by Paul Waggott via Telegraph Office, 2026-04-26.

docs.title: Agent Tatum Black
docs.text: [!info] At a Glance Role: Twilight Legion Agent, Seattle Location: Grand Central Hotel, Seattle Faction: Twilight Legion Status: Alive (recurring)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Handler for Father Miller, Mama Duvall, and Jim in Seattle, first encountered in Seattle, October 1884. Young, nervous Minnesotan running the local Twilight Legion office alone after both his colleagues were killed. Offered $10/day and $1,000 each on completion. Gave them the list of strange events to investigate. Based at the Grand Central Hotel. Competent despite the tinhorn energy — his mind is quick and he holds the line on the law.

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Average size, average features, average clothes — easy to miss in a crowd, which is just what the Agency looks for. Brown hair. Perpetually nervous energy offset by genuine determination. Always fidgeting with his bowler hat when he talks. Speaks clearly but sometimes shudders mid-sentence when recalling something bad.

docs.title: Background
docs.text:
A young, overwhelmed Minnesotan now running the Seattle Agency office alone. Three agents were stationed here two weeks before the campaign begins. James was eaten by a rat swarm. Samantha Watson was gunned down by a Harrowed outlaw named Spider Moore. Black is what's left.

Recruited Father Miller, Mama Duvall, and Jim through Tombstone Epitaph reporter and Twilight Legion contact Lacy O'Malley. Also invited Dr. Eliza Crowe to assist with her experimental phobometer.

Pays $10/day for expenses and offers $1,000 each on completion of their task.

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text: Keep Seattle from sliding into a Deadland until reinforcements arrive — which could be months. He's in over his head and he knows it. Not too proud to ask for help.

docs.title: Personality
docs.text:
Nervous but sharp. His mind is quick despite the tinhorn energy. Holds the line on legality — he will help those he works with out of minor "misunderstandings" but won't tolerate unjustified violence or mischief. Delivers dry, self-aware humor about his own situation.

"You'll need lots of ammo for this job. And a good umbrella."

docs.title: Role in Campaign
docs.text:
• Act One: Primary handler in Seattle. Provides the base at the Grand Central, the task list, and the payment structure.
  • Act Two: Sends Father Miller, Mama Duvall, and Jim to meet Ranger Strnisa in Enumclaw.
  • Act Three: Named as a potential "victim" in the Bone King's trials — if a hero takes a fur coat, Agent Black is one who suffers.

docs.title: Stat Block
docs.text:
Uses standard Agency profile. Average civilian stats — he is not a combatant.

Attributes: Agility d6, Smarts d8, Spirit d6, Strength d6, Vigor d6 Skills: Common Knowledge d8, Notice d8, Persuasion d8, Research d8, Stealth d8 Pace: 6 | Parry: 4 | Toughness: 5 Hindrances: Cautious, Loyal

  • Dr. Eliza Crowe — Invited to Seattle specifically; partners on phobometer calibration
  • Samantha Watson — His dead partner; killed by Spider Moore
  • James — His other dead partner; killed by a rat swarm

docs.title: Annie Paige
docs.text: [!info] At a Glance Role: Archaeologist / Explorer Location: Seattle Faction: Independent Status: Alive

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: First encountered in a Seattle saloon in October 1884. Drunk, recently expelled from the Royal Geographic Society, and carrying what appeared to be an archaeological skull fragment of unusual provenance. Introduced herself at length. Brilliant and chaotic. Recurring contact.

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Short brown hair, khaki pants, yellow top, blue scarf. Pith helmet. Carries an archaeology kit and a Colt Rainmaker. Usually slightly drunk when first encountered. Looks younger than she is.

docs.title: Background
docs.text:
Born in Massachusetts. Worked with her father in archaeology from childhood. Educated at Oxford. Royal Geographic Society membership recently revoked — she's furious about it and will tell you why at length, whether you asked or not.

Has a Necronomicon skull fragment in her bag. Believes she found proof of alien structures at Cahokia. Nobody believes her. She may be right.

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text: Prove everyone who doubted her wrong. Find the thing that can't exist. She's brilliant and chaotic and impossible to stop once she's locked onto something.

docs.title: Personality
docs.text: Loud. Funny. Incapable of leaving anything alone. Gets drunk and overshares classified archaeological secrets. Completely fearless in the way that only people who haven't fully processed their own mortality are.

docs.title: Played Version
docs.text: → [[Wiki/Played/NPCs/Annie Paige]]

docs.title: Deputy Chandra Lawson
docs.text: [!info] At a Glance Role: Deputy Sheriff, Seattle Location: Seattle Faction: Law Status: Alive

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Deputy Sheriff, Seattle. First encountered during the Sack-Headed Man investigation, late October 1884. Direct, competent, genuinely friendly. Will assist with investigations but needs official grounds or a trusted favour — she can't act without cause. Carries a Colt Lightning and a club. Has a slight Haitian influence in her speech from her grandmother. Good to have on your side.

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The almost always cheery Deputy hails from Kansas with a thick country accent — and an occasional Haitian influence she picked up from her "grams," the same woman who taught her voodoo. Curious to a fault. Asks detailed questions about ongoing investigations, how a creature was defeated, what ammo was used. She's genuinely a best friend to those who let her be. Carries a Colt Lightning and a club.

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text: Keep Seattle safe. She's good at this job and she knows it. Doesn't need help — but she'll take it when offered, which puts anyone working with her in the complicated position of being useful and unofficial.

docs.title: Personality
docs.text: Direct. Dry. Loyal to people who prove they deserve it. Will tell you exactly what she thinks and what she can and cannot do, and won't apologize for either.

docs.title: Background
docs.text: From Kansas. Haitian voodoo tradition passed down from her grandmother — she keeps this quiet but it informs how she reads a scene. Pushing for the title of Assistant Chief of Police; Woolery hasn't agreed yet.

docs.title: Played Version
docs.text: → [[Wiki/Played/NPCs/Deputy Chandra Lawson]]

docs.title: Dr. Eliza Crowe
docs.text: [!info] At a Glance Role: Scientist, Twilight Legion Agent Location: Seattle Faction: Twilight Legion Status: Alive

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: First encountered in the Grand Central Hotel lobby, October 1884. A scientist and Twilight Legion contact who came to Seattle to track the city's rising Fear Level with her experimental phobometer — a brass-and-glass instrument with a twitching needle that measures ambient fear energy. She explained the device to those present. Also witnessed being harassed by O'Neil gang members before the confrontation was resolved. Precise, focused, and not to be underestimated.

docs.title: Description
docs.text: 54 years old. Born a slave in Louisiana. Attained freedom and became both a medical doctor and a practitioner of the New Science. Carries her phobometer — a device she built to measure Fear Level — and a derringer.

docs.title: Background
docs.text:
After barely surviving a supernatural encounter in New Orleans, she was recruited by the Twilight Legion. Learned about the Reckoning and the role of fear. Came to Seattle specifically to measure and combat the rising Fear Level she detected.

Perfects her phobometer during the Bloodsucking Fiends encounter — the device gets its first accurate reading when the vampire threat is resolved.

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text: Science first. Measure it, understand it, fix it. She believes the Fear Level can be managed if you can quantify it. She's right.

docs.title: Personality
docs.text: Precise. Impatient with superstition despite operating in a world of the supernatural — she distinguishes carefully between "unexplained" and "inexplicable." Warm to people who take her seriously. Cutting to people who don't.

docs.title: Stat Block (Book p.129)
docs.text: Attributes: Agility d6, Smarts d10, Spirit d6, Strength d4, Vigor d6 Skills: Academics d6, Athletics d4, Common Knowledge d8, Driving d6, Healing d10, Notice d8, Persuasion d6, Repair d8, Science d8, Shooting d6, Stealth d4, Weird Science d10 Pace: 6 | Parry: 2 | Toughness: 5 Hindrances: Curious, Madness (Delusion), Quirk (never goes anywhere without Tweety) Edges: Arcane Background (Mad Scientist), Gadgeteer Powers: Burst (ether-condenser), sloth/speed (chrono-valve). PP: 25 Gear: Gadgets, lab coat, goggles, tool kit

docs.title: Tweety
docs.text: Dr. Crowe's canary — never goes anywhere without him. Size –4, Toughness 1. Has seen things.

docs.title: The Phobometer
docs.text:
A metal rod about 10 inches long, hollow with a clear glass window. Six marks along the glass, filled with murky black liquid. Measures ambient Fear energy. Currently uncalibrated — see [[Wiki/Canon/Lore/The Phobometer]] for full mechanics.

The missing calibration ingredient: the blood of a supernaturally evil being. Resolved at the end of Bloodsucking Fiends. After that, reads accurately. Will spike to 6 at the Bone King's domain in Act Three.

docs.title: First Appearance
docs.text:
First seen in the Grand Central lobby, beating an O'Neil goon with her wet umbrella.

"It's DOCTOR Crowe, and I'll not hear of it!"

docs.title: Played Version
docs.text: → [[Wiki/Played/NPCs/Dr. Eliza Crowe]]

docs.title: Fanny Starling
docs.text: [!info] At a Glance Role: Opera Diva Location: Frye's Opera House, Seattle Faction: Civilian Status: Alive

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The star performer at Frye's Opera House. First encountered October 1884. She believed the opera house was haunted — she'd been hearing sounds from beneath the stage when she practiced. The investigation revealed not a ghost but Krista's orphan gang sneaking through the tunnels below to listen to the music. Left on good terms. Well-connected in Seattle's wealthier circles.

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The opera's star performer. An "amazing performer" by any description. Believes the opera house is haunted — specifically, that she hears things moving around beneath the stage when she practices.

docs.title: Background
docs.text: She's right about the sounds. Krista's orphan gang sneaks through tunnels beneath the opera house into a space under the stage and listens whenever someone performs. They're not malicious — just captivated by the music.

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text: Perform. Be believed. She wants someone to take the haunting seriously.

docs.title: Key Interactions
docs.text:
• Investigation of the "haunting" revealed Krista's gang rather than a ghost
  • Fanny was relieved, confused, and possibly charmed by the orphans
  • A useful high-society contact for anyone needing access to Seattle's wealthier circles

docs.text: Head cook at the Grand Central Hotel. First encountered during the Grand Central Hotel investigation, late October 1884. docs.title: H.P. Lovelace
docs.text: [!info] NPC — Player Created An in-world author of horror and romance fiction, based in Providence, Rhode Island. Created by Stalker Jack (Mama Duvall's player) as part of Mama Duvall's backstory. Mama Duvall reads his work extensively.

docs.title: Character Notes
docs.text: A writer of dark, atmospheric fiction. Health uncertain. Signs correspondence simply as "Lovelace, Providence." Replies are brief, formal, and slightly ominous in tone — the pen of a man who lives too close to whatever he writes about.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text: Character Notes Mama Duvall Fan and correspondent. Lovelace received her message warmly.

docs.title: Telegraph Exchange — 2026-04-26
docs.text:
Mama Duvall sent: Fan message praising his work and wishing him good health; hoping his next novel is not far away.

Response: MAMA DE VALL SEATTLE STOP YOUR KIND WORDS RECEIVED WITH GREAT PLEASURE STOP THE DARK MUSES ARE RESTLESS AND THE NEXT TALE STIRS IN THE SHADOWS STOP HEALTH UNCERTAIN BUT THE PEN DOES NOT REST STOP PROVIDENCE WATCHES OVER US ALL STOP LOVELACE PROVIDENCE RHODE ISLAND STOP

docs.title: GM Notes
docs.text:
• Pure character development — no plot relevance. Bot can handle freely.
  • If Mama Duvall writes again, Lovelace can respond in this voice: world-weary, literary, slightly gothic.
  • Keep him in Providence — no reason for him to come west.

docs.title: Horace Clayton
docs.text: [!info] At a Glance Role: Reporter, Seattle Post-Intelligencer Location: Seattle Faction: The Press Status: Alive

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Reporter for the Seattle Post-Intelligencer. First encountered late October 1884 when Father Miller, Mama Duvall, and Jim gave him a Tale-Tellin' interview about the Sack-Headed Man. Published the account; Fear Level dropped. Gave Father Miller a fair write-up after the Batsquatch encounter on November 3rd. Friendly — will trade information for a good story. Remembers everything.

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Wiry. Always has a notebook. Never quite seems to be paying attention and always is. Drinks moderately. Remembers everything.

docs.title: Background
docs.text:
Has been covering Seattle since before it was worth covering. Knows where most bodies are buried — figuratively. A few literally, after the last few weeks.

Works under Editor Thomas Prosch and Owner Leigh Hunt at the Post-Intelligencer.

docs.title: Voice
docs.text:
Dry wit. Victorian propriety with a raised eyebrow underneath it. Prints the official line but includes details that make the reader think. Never lies — just selects. Will describe a supernatural event in language that sounds mundane while including every detail that makes it obviously not.

"The conductor maintains it was merely a freak bush leaping from the tracks in the dead of night."

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text: The truth. But more practically, a good story. He's not reckless — he won't print something that gets someone killed. But he's watching everything and writing it all down somewhere.

docs.title: Personality
docs.text: Professionally warm. Remembers your name, your drink, what you said three weeks ago. Asks questions that sound like small talk. Will absolutely print the thing you said off the record if it's interesting enough and you didn't say "off the record" first.

docs.title: Background (from Book)
docs.text:
Seattle's first African American journalist. Covers politics and occasionally stranger stories. A trusted ally of Tombstone Epitaph reporter Lacy O'Malley.

Works under Editor Thomas Prosch (taciturn; only interested in facts; at odds with Clayton's instincts but defers to ownership) and Owner Leigh Hunt (bullish on sharing information and revealing truth; frequent thorn in the Agency's side).

Agent Tatum Black works with Clayton occasionally — helping him find the line between reporting the truth and sending the public into an outright panic.

The Post-Intelligencer building is on the northeast corner of Yesler Way and Post Street.

docs.title: Jerome Bianchi
docs.text: [!info] At a Glance Role: Hotel Manager, Grand Central Hotel Location: Grand Central Hotel, Seattle Faction: Civilian Status: Alive

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Manager of the Grand Central Hotel — the current base of operations in Seattle. First encountered during the Grand Central Hotel investigation, late October 1884. Resistant to wall demolition at the time; quietly grateful once Giuseppe Vivaldi was laid to rest. Now a reliable, discreet contact. Connected to Seattle's Italian community.

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Compact, professional Italian-American man. Well-dressed, precise. Has managed the Grand Central for eleven years. Radiates practiced calm and professional hospitality.

docs.title: Background
docs.text: Born to Italian immigrants. Grandmother from Naples — he speaks Italian fluently. Has managed the Grand Central since 1873. Was aware of the haunting by Giuseppe Vivaldi for years but kept it quiet to protect the hotel's reputation.

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text: Protect the hotel. Protect its reputation. Keep things running smoothly. He's not a bad man — just a pragmatic one.

docs.title: Personality
docs.text: Deflects with hospitality. Offers food when things get uncomfortable. Not dishonest exactly — just extremely selective about what he volunteers. Warms up considerably once he trusts someone.

docs.title: Staff
docs.text:
• Camille Broad — assistant manager; helps watch the desk and keep the books
  • Giuseppe Marinetti — hotel cook; researching Salish elk mythology at the Priest's request
  • Half-dozen maintenance staff and maids

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Italian community — well connected, respected
  • Giuseppe Marinetti — hotel cook, trusted staff member

docs.title: Krista
docs.text: [!info] At a Glance Role: Leader, Orphan Gang Location: Seattle tunnels, Frye's Opera House area Faction: Street Children Status: Alive

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Leader of a gang of orphaned street children who survive by their wits in Seattle. First encountered October 1884 during the Frye's Opera House investigation — her gang had been sneaking through the tunnels beneath the building to listen to Fanny Starling perform. They were the source of the "haunting." Not malicious — just captivated by the music. The only adults who know where they are and what they're doing are Father Miller, Mama Duvall, and Jim.

docs.title: Description
docs.text: A girl. Age not specified — old enough to lead, young enough that anyone with a conscience will think twice. Resourceful, sharp, and fiercely protective of her group.

docs.title: Background
docs.text: Leads a gang of orphaned street children who survive by their wits in Seattle. They: - Steal food from grocery stores (the missing inventory at Cosper McIntyre's that no one can explain) - Sneak through tunnels beneath the opera house to listen to the performers from a space under the stage - Are connected to the Seattle Children's Home outreach (which hasn't found them a permanent building yet)

docs.title: Role in Campaign
docs.text:
• Mentioned in the Frye's Opera House "haunting" (the sounds Fanny Starling hears)
  • Detailed in Little Annie Orphaned (p.57)
  • The orphans are thieves but not violent — anyone with a moral compass should feel protective of them

docs.title: Lacy O'Malley
docs.text: [!info] At a Glance Role: Reporter, Tombstone Epitaph Location: Tombstone, Arizona Territory (based); travels Faction: The Press (Tombstone Epitaph) Status: Alive

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Reporter for the Tombstone Epitaph. She's the reason Father Miller, Mama Duvall, and Jim came to Seattle — she reached out on their arrival in Seattle, October 1884, on behalf of Agent Black and the Twilight Legion and arranged the introduction. Has not appeared in person; her role is as a trusted off-screen recommender. Ally of Horace Clayton.

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The Tombstone Epitaph's supernatural-beat reporter. Known across the Weird West as a trusted voice on the strange and dangerous. Has seen enough that almost nothing rattles her anymore.

docs.title: Background
docs.text:
Reporter for the Tombstone Epitaph — the paper that covers the Weird West's supernatural events with more candor than most. Trusted ally of Horace Clayton. The two share sources, methodology, and a mutual understanding of the line between informing the public and sparking a panic.

She thinks Leigh Hunt sometimes crosses that line. She's said so directly. They're still on speaking terms.

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text: The truth — but responsibly. She's made the same calculation as Clayton: some details can be printed, some can't, and you have to know which is which before you sit down to write.

docs.title: Role in Campaign
docs.text:
Primarily an off-screen presence — a name that establishes how the PI fits into the larger Weird West press network. If she appears in Seattle, it means something significant enough to draw a reporter from Tombstone.

When she does appear, she's a useful ally: well-connected, credible, experienced with the supernatural, and not naive about what the Agency is or what it does.

docs.title: Relationship with Clayton
docs.text: Peers, not rivals. They share information when it helps and hold back when it doesn't. Clayton trusts her judgment; she trusts his.

docs.title: Liam O'Neil
docs.text: [!info] At a Glance Role: Irish Gang Boss, protection racketeer Location: O'Neil's Irish Pub, Pioneer Square area Faction: O'Neil Gang Status: Alive (recurring antagonist)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Irish gang boss operating in Seattle. Members of his gang were encountered harassing Dr. Eliza Crowe in October 1884 and driven off. The O'Neil gang are known as thugs — connected to someone, operating in Seattle, best avoided or confronted carefully. Liam O'Neil's name and the full scope of his operation are not yet widely known.

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Usually found at his private table in the back corner of his pub, or standing at the bar chatting, or upstairs in his office. Almost always present — he doesn't hide from trouble. Carries a derringer and a knife but prefers persuasion and Jacko Johnson for the rough stuff.

docs.title: Background
docs.text:
Came from Ireland with his sister Mary a few years ago. Had trouble in New York and Chicago before fleeing west to Seattle. Vowed not to run again.

Set up a loan-sharking and protection racket in the booming city. His operation is just legitimate enough to keep him out of jail — merchants genuinely do need security in a boomtown, and when clients get beaten for missed payments, O'Neil makes the cases disappear through threats, false witnesses, or bribery.

His sister Mary had a falling out with him and now works at the Emerald Island brothel, where she's become addicted to opium. Dentist Jenny Johanson treats her free of charge and knows who she is.

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text: Get rich. Stay free. Seattle is his and he intends to keep it that way.

docs.title: Personality
docs.text: Genuinely charming in a way that makes it easy to forget he's a criminal. Charismatic, gambling-hall smooth. Ruthless when crossed. Keeps at least five enforcers around till 3 a.m.

docs.title: Stat Block
docs.text: Attributes: Agility d8, Smarts d8, Spirit d8, Strength d6, Vigor d6 Skills: Athletics d6, Common Knowledge d8, Fighting d6, Gambling d8, Intimidation d8, Notice d8, Persuasion d10, Shooting d4, Stealth d8, Thievery d8 Pace: 6 | Parry: 5 | Toughness: 5 Hindrances: Greedy (Major), Mean, Ruthless (Major) Edges: Alertness, Charismatic, Command, Elan, Guts, Luck, Rich, Thief Gear: Derringer (Range 3/6/12, Damage 2d4), knife (Str+d4)

docs.title: His Forces
docs.text:
• 5 enforcers at the pub nightly
  • 2d6 hangers-on on short notice
  • 4d6 thugs with an hour's notice
  • ~100 men with a few days and money

docs.title: Key Associates
docs.text:
• Jacko Johnson — primary enforcer; silver wolf-head cane
  • Mary O'Neil — estranged sister; Emerald Island brothel
  • Jenny Johanson — dentist who pulls teeth for the gang (gold fillings from bodies)

docs.title: Role in Campaign
docs.text: Recurring low-level antagonist throughout Act One. His gang resurfaces repeatedly. The Fightin' Irish encounter (p.56) escalates through several confrontations culminating in the Emerald Island fire.

docs.title: Thomas Prosch
docs.text: [!info] At a Glance Role: Editor in Chief, Seattle Post-Intelligencer Location: Seattle Post-Intelligencer, Yesler Way & Post Street Faction: The Press Status: Alive

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Editor in Chief of the Seattle Post-Intelligencer. Met during the Sack-Headed Man investigation, late October 1884, when Father Miller, Mama Duvall, and Jim came to the newspaper for information. Taciturn, facts-only, not given to dramatic speculation. Cooperative as long as you can source your claims. Works with Horace Clayton, though they have ongoing professional disagreements about how stories should be framed.

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Taciturn. Interested only in facts. Unimpressed by instinct, implication, or dramatic effect. If a story can't be sourced, it shouldn't run. This puts him at chronic odds with his best reporter.

docs.title: Background
docs.text:
Editor in chief of the PI. Professionally and personally at odds with Horace Clayton over how stories should be framed and what they should imply. He loses these arguments more often than he wins — Leigh Hunt tends to side with Clayton, so Prosch's practical power is to tone down stories rather than kill them outright.

He exercises that power. Stories that would set the city on fire in Clayton's draft come out measured and careful in print — but every key detail is still there for a reader who's paying attention.

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text: Accurate reporting. A clean editorial record. Institutional integrity. He's not wrong about any of these things — he just applies them in a way that occasionally lets important truths die of starvation.

docs.title: Personality
docs.text: Dry. Economy of words. Doesn't volunteer opinions unless pressed. More self-aware than he appears — he knows the paper's reputation comes from Clayton and Hunt, not from him, and he's made his peace with it.

docs.title: Key Interactions
docs.text:
• To verify a fact or find a historical record through the paper, Prosch is the person to go through
  • More cooperative than Hunt with the Agency — not an ally, but not hostile to the idea of holding certain things back
  • A Persuasion roll (no penalty) gets him to flag a story for review before it runs; he'll push back on anything he can't independently verify

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A secret organisation operating across the West, dedicated to investigating and suppressing supernatural threats. Operatives work independently in the field; the Legion provides resources, intelligence, and backup when justified.

docs.title: Contacting the Legion
docs.text:
Requests can be sent to the Legion via telegraph. Responses come from a regional handler — a Legion coordinator based in the Pacific Northwest. Tone: terse, professional, cautious. The Legion does not waste words and does not commit resources without justification.

Handler telegraph identity: LEGION NORTHWEST RELAY

docs.title: What the Legion Can Provide
docs.text: Resource Availability Notes Intelligence Case-by-case Information on known threats, entities, or persons of interest Backup Requires justification Field operatives; not dispatched lightly Equipment Requires requisition Specialised gear for supernatural threats Extraction Emergency only Getting a compromised operative out Authorisation GM decision Formal backing for sensitive operations

docs.title: GM Notes
docs.text:
• NPC membership is forbidden territory for the bot. If a player asks whether a specific NPC is Legion, the handler deflects: "Operational security. That information is not transmitted by wire."
  • Use Legion responses to give the party direction without railroading — hints, not orders.
  • Legion requests that touch on main plot content (Bone King, Fear Machine, etc.) should be flagged to #marshal-desk for GM response rather than bot-generated.

docs.title: Capitol Hill
docs.text: [!info] At a Glance Type: District / Neighbourhood Location: Seattle Status: Active

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
A large hill on Seattle's eastern edge. Visited during the Sack-Headed Man investigation, late October 1884.

Notable: the hill was set aside for the state capital and then the university. A cemetery here was relocated in February 1884 — a mismanaged process that left many unmarked graves, including a mass pauper's grave at the southeastern foot of the hill. The area is now deforested, with thick blackberry bushes covering the former grave sites.

Cletus's old house — an abandoned property here was the former home of the Sack-Headed Man. It was investigated as part of the case. The Brown family (Jenny and Laurie) live across the street.

docs.title: Frye's Opera House
docs.text: [!info] At a Glance Type: Opera House Location: Seattle Status: Active

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Investigated in October 1884. The opera house had been plagued by mysterious wails, thumping from the rafters, and extinguished gaslights. The investigation revealed the source was not a ghost but Krista's orphan gang — street children who had found a way through the tunnels beneath the building to listen to Fanny Starling perform from a space under the stage.

The "haunting" was resolved without incident. The children were not harmed or punished.

Key people here: - [[Fanny Starling]] — the opera's star performer; asked for the investigation - [[Krista]] — orphan gang leader; her group used the tunnels beneath the stage

docs.title: Grand Central Hotel
docs.text: [!info] At a Glance Type: Three-story hotel Address: Commercial Street, downtown Seattle Manager: Jerome Bianchi Role: Home base throughout Act One

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
A modern, three-story building (all stairs, no elevator). Clean, well-maintained, and above the average for Seattle. Agent Tatum Black has secured rooms here for Father Miller, Mama Duvall, and Jim — covered by Agency expenses unless they choose to go elsewhere.

The hotel is the base of operations for Act One. It's also where Dr. Eliza Crowe was first encountered (in the lobby, beating an O'Neil goon with her umbrella).

docs.title: Staff
docs.text: Person Role Notes Jerome Bianchi Manager Friendly, excitable Italian-American; reluctant to cause trouble; loyal once trust is earned Camille Broad Assistant Manager Helps watch the desk and keep the books Giuseppe Marinetti Cook Italian community member; researching Salish elk mythology at the Priest's request Lavinia LaVerne Maid First to alert to trouble in the lobby (Fear For All opener) Half-dozen maintenance staff and maids — —

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
Ground Floor: Lobby, front desk, restaurant entrance Second Floor: Guest rooms Third Floor: Guest rooms; Agent Black's suite (where the first meeting with him took place) Fourth Floor: Additional rooms

The book includes floor plan maps for all four floors (p.40–41).

docs.title: The Haunting (Resolved)
docs.text:
The hotel was haunted by Giuseppe Vivaldi — a carpenter entombed in the walls during construction in 1880. His spirit had been trapped there since, growing increasingly mad. Father Miller, Mama Duvall, and Jim resolved this in late October 1884, laying him to rest and returning his toolbelt to his family.

Result: The aid of Seattle's Italian community was gained. Bianchi is quietly grateful and a reliable ally.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Fear For All — first scene; O'Neil goon confrontation in the lobby; Dr. Crowe introduction
  • Haunted Hotel — the Vivaldi ghost investigation
  • Post-Credit Scene (Campaign End) — A mysterious man leaves a badge with a bullet hole and a card reading "Stone"

docs.title: Seattle Post-Intelligencer
docs.text: [!info] At a Glance Type: Newspaper Address: Northeast corner of Yesler Way and Post Street Faction: The Press Also called: The PI

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Built on the "graves" of several predecessor newspapers. The Post-Intelligencer is now Seattle's leading paper — progressive, hard-hitting, and a frequent irritant to the Agency and every other institution that would prefer certain things go unreported.

Its reputation comes directly from its ownership. Leigh Hunt runs the paper with a heavy bias toward transparency and truth, which filters down through the entire editorial operation whether Thomas Prosch approves or not.

docs.title: Staff
docs.text:
Name Role File Leigh Hunt Owner [[Wiki/Canon/NPCs/Leigh Hunt]] Thomas Prosch Editor in Chief [[Wiki/Canon/NPCs/Thomas Prosch]] Horace Clayton Reporter (politics / strange stories) [[Wiki/Canon/NPCs/Horace Clayton]]

Agent Tatum Black works with Clayton occasionally — see [[Wiki/Canon/NPCs/Agent Tatum Black]].

Lacy O'Malley (Tombstone Epitaph) is Clayton's trusted out-of-town ally — see [[Wiki/Canon/NPCs/Lacy O'Malley]].

docs.title: Role in Campaign
docs.text:
The PI is the primary interface with public perception for Father Miller, Mama Duvall, and Jim. What gets printed shapes how Seattle sees their actions — and how much heat they attract from law, gangsters, and frightened civilians.

The paper is also an intelligence asset. Clayton is quietly accumulating information they don't know he has. Hunt will print things the Agency desperately wishes he wouldn't. Prosch tries to put the brakes on and usually fails.

docs.title: Tension at the PI
docs.text: The three-way dynamic between Hunt (print everything), Prosch (only verifiable facts), and Clayton (print the truth in ways that make readers think without starting a panic) is the internal engine of the paper. The party's relationship with each of them will determine what gets printed — and how.

docs.title: The Agency Problem
docs.text: Hunt considers the Agency an obstacle to truth. He'll print things that compromise operations if he believes the public has a right to know. Even Lacy O'Malley — no friend to secrecy herself — thinks Hunt sometimes goes too far. Agent Black spends real effort managing this relationship to prevent full disclosure of the supernatural.

docs.title: Yesler-Leery Building
docs.text: [!info] At a Glance Type: Commercial building Address: Pioneer Place, Seattle Status: Active

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
A large commercial building on Pioneer Place. The rooftop was accessed in November 1884 to deal with a devil bat nest — five devil bats including a Devil Bat Queen (locally called "Batsquatch") had roosted there and were hunting lone pedestrians in the fog. The threat was eliminated.

Key people here: - [[George Venable Smith]] — attorney with a large, well-appointed office on the upper floors. Not yet formally met.
